# INFRASTRUCTURE DRIFT — the live Caddyfile is NOT generated by this role's template

**Measured:** 2026-10-14, on `vps2` (a.k.a. `testserver2`, `23.182.128.51`, FIPS mesh alias `vps2fips`).

## The finding

| | value |
|---|---|
| Live Caddyfile | `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` — **1066 lines, 24 vhosts** |
| Template in this role | `ansible/roles/caddy/templates/Caddyfile.http.j2` — **469 lines** |
| Running process | `caddy run --environ --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile` as a **bare binary** (`/usr/bin/caddy`) |
| What the role assumes | a **Docker** container built from `caddy/Dockerfile`, config at `/opt/tollgate/caddy/Caddyfile` |

So the role's template does not produce the live config, and the role's deployment mechanism
(container) is not what is running. **Deploying this role's template over the live file would
DESTROY roughly 14 working production vhosts.**

Vhosts present live but absent from the template include: `agent-test`, `ai`, `blossom2`,
`ci`, `contextvm.sovereignengineering.io`, `continuum-test`, `cvm-pwa`, `friends`, `market-agg`,
`market-wot`, `matrix`, `mint`, `mint-test`, `nostrhackday`, `poc`,
`proxy.sovereignengineering.io`, `relay`, `relay2`, `routstr`, `stackstr`, `test-fips`, and the
three `plebeian.orangesync.tech` vhosts. Several are `reverse_proxy` routes to live services.

## Consequence for this repo

`ansible/roles/caddy` is **not currently the source of truth for the live reverse proxy**. Any
`--tags caddy` run against `m2` is a production-destructive operation. Until that drift is
resolved, the role must be treated as **aspirational**, and changes to the live proxy must be
made surgically with a validated reload (see below).

## What was done for `portal.orangesync.tech` (the safe path)

Because deploying the template was destructive and deploying nothing was unmanaged, the vhost
was added **surgically**, with the declaration still committed to this repo as the intent:

1. `sudo cp -n /etc/caddy/Caddyfile /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.bak-$TS` — backup taken first.
   NOTE: an earlier invocation in the same session wrote a literal `$TS` in the filename
   because the variable did not expand inside the quoted heredoc. The file is a valid backup;
   only its name is wrong. Recorded so nobody mistakes it for a real timestamped snapshot.
2. Append the vhost block (byte-identical to the block this repo's template emits for the
   `tollgate_portal` role, minus Jinja substitution) via `tee -a`.
3. `sudo caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile` → **"Valid configuration"**.
4. `sudo systemctl reload caddy` — a reload, never a restart, so existing connections drain.
5. `mkdir -p /srv/tollgate/tollgate-portal`, chown to the caddy user, write a placeholder
   `index.html` so the vhost is provably serving rather than merely configured.

## Verification actually observed

```
$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code} tls=%{ssl_verify_result}\n' https://portal.orangesync.tech/
HTTP 200 tls_verify=0
```

`tls_verify_result=0` means the certificate chain validated against the SYSTEM trust store — a
real publicly-trusted certificate, not a click-through. Confirmed at the cert level:

```
issuer=C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = YE1
subject=CN = portal.orangesync.tech
notBefore=Oct 14 17:52:16 2026 GMT
notAfter=Jan 12 17:52:15 2027 GMT
```

Security headers observed on the response: `referrer-policy`, `x-content-type-options`.
(Caddy reports its own `server:` banner; the template's `-Server` directive is in the committed
block but the live block was written without it — a deliberate inconsistency to reconcile when
the template is made authoritative. Flagged, not silently matched.)

## How to reconcile (a real task, not done here)

Pick ONE and make it true:

- **(A) Adopt the live file into the repo.** Diff the live 1066-line file against the template,
  parameterise the extra vhosts (they are mostly `reverse_proxy localhost:<port>` routes to
  services this repo already deploys), and commit the result. Then the role becomes the source
  of truth and `--tags caddy` is safe again. **This is the correct end state.**
- **(B) Retire the role.** If Caddy is managed by hand on these hosts, delete the role rather
  than leaving a destructive trap in the repo.

Until either is done, treat `ansible/roles/caddy` as **aspirational**, and note that the
`tollgate_portal` role entry added to `group_vars/m2.yml` and `group_vars/m1.yml` will only take
effect once the role actually drives the live config.
